title: Match the Tool to the Thought
hook: Chat is not the only shape. Hire the interface that fits the cognitive job.
excerpt: A one-screen contrast: linear chat vs spatial workspace when thoughts need to branch.
lede: Most AI clients are messaging apps. Some thinking jobs need cards, parks, and forks instead of one scrolling transcript.
author: Nitish Chauhan

left.label: Linear chat
left.body: One thread. Good for bounded Q and A. Bad when three thoughts want the floor at once.

right.label: Spatial desk
right.body: Sessions, bubbles, park and pin. You keep the narrative without forcing parallel ideas into a queue.

modules.intro: Flip between two modes. Notice which job each one is actually good at.
modules.whatToDo: 1. Toggle the mode. 2. Read the signal that changes.
modules.writerRule: So on the page, name the cognitive job before you pick the tool.
modules.soFar: Interface shape is a hiring decision, not a brand loyalty test.

data.leftBody: Clarify, fetch, implement a bounded task.

takeaway: Stop asking which AI is best. Ask which interface fits the thought you are having.
caveat: Illustrative contrast, not a product review.
ogAlt: Match the Tool to the Thought
